Nursing Theories

Nursing theories — Nightingale, Peplau, Orem, Henderson, Roy and their application.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Name major nursing theorists and their theories
  • Describe Orem’s self-care theory
  • Explain how nursing theories guide practice

In simple words

Nursing theories give a framework for understanding what nurses do and why. They guide assessment, care planning and evaluation.

Major theorists: Nightingale (environment), Peplau (nurse–patient relationship), Orem (self-care), Henderson (14 basic needs), Roy (adaptation).

Major nursing theories

Theorist Theory Key idea
Nightingale Environmental theory Clean air, light, warmth, cleanliness, quiet, food
Peplau Interpersonal relations Nurse–patient relationship in phases
Orem Self-care deficit Nurses help when patients cannot care for themselves
Henderson 14 basic needs Assist with 14 fundamental needs
Roy Adaptation model Help the person adapt to changes

Orem’s self-care deficit theory

  • Self-care — activities a person does to maintain health.
  • Self-care deficit — when a person cannot meet their own needs.
  • Nursing system — wholly compensatory, partly compensatory or supportive-educative.

🔴 Orem’s key idea

Orem: nurses help when patients cannot meet their own self-care needs. The nurse’s system is wholly compensatory, partly compensatory or supportive-educative.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Assessment — use theories to organise data collection.
  • Care planning — choose interventions based on theory (e.g., Orem: how much help does the patient need?).
  • Environment — apply Nightingale: clean, quiet, well-ventilated wards.
  • Relationship — apply Peplau: build trust through the phases of the relationship.
  • Evaluation — check whether the patient’s needs are met.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Nursing theories give a framework for practice.
  2. Nightingale: environment (air, light, warmth, cleanliness, quiet, food).
  3. Peplau: nurse–patient relationship in phases.
  4. Orem: self-care deficit — nurse helps when the patient cannot self-care.
  5. Henderson: assist with 14 basic needs; Roy: adaptation.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Orem’s nursing systems: wholly compensatory, partly compensatory, supportive-educative.
  2. Theories guide assessment, planning and evaluation.
  3. Apply theory to individualise care.
  4. Theories are used in education, research and practice.

📌 Memory trick

Theorists: “N-P-O-H-R” — Nightingale, Peplau, Orem, Henderson, Roy.

60-second revision

  • Nursing theories guide practice.
  • Nightingale = environment; Peplau = relationship.
  • Orem = self-care deficit; nurse helps when patient cannot.
  • Henderson = 14 basic needs; Roy = adaptation.
  • Orem’s systems: wholly/partly/supportive-educative.

Test yourself

Orem’s theory focuses on:

Answer: B. Orem’s self-care deficit theory focuses on when a patient cannot meet their own self-care needs.

Nightingale’s theory focuses on:

Answer: B. Nightingale’s environmental theory focuses on clean air, light, warmth, cleanliness, quiet and food.

Peplau’s theory focuses on:

Answer: A. Peplau’s theory centres on the nurse–patient interpersonal relationship.

Henderson identified:

Answer: A. Henderson’s theory is built around 14 basic nursing needs.

Roy’s theory focuses on:

Answer: A. Roy’s adaptation model focuses on helping the person adapt to changes.
